I know that discussions are ok according to this

groups.google.com/g/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/c/ma8z8iBgHEU/m/j6EWZ_p_1iAJ

Messages.Author: Pudel
Messages.Body:
I feel like more appropriate phrasing of this question is:
1) Is the moment when seating is chosen part of the game?
2) What (if any) discussion is allowed during seating between players?
Examples:
Player A tells Player B that if they choose to sit as Player’s A predator, they will rush their vampires from turn 1 and will not allow them to play and therefore encourages them to sit somewhere else.

Player A asks if they sit crosstable from player B, will they be generally supportive for each other when voting.

Player A offers Player B to sit as their predator and not go forward until they score a VP in exchange for a genuine attempt from player B to get VP as fast as possible. Rationale being - Player A can’t deal with B’s prey on their own (e.g. too much intercept, vote lock etc.)

Players are aware of a particularly explosive deck on the table, e.g. Tupdogs, Chameleon, Clow Car and discuss of there is a way to sit that will help them against such deck and what that would entail, e.g. Player A (vote deck) offers Player B (block deck) to deal damage crosstable against their prey if they sit next to Clown Car player and block their Embraces.

Etc etc

The point being - all of the above would have been generally acceptable during the game as pretty standard deals, I would presume. Would the same be allowed during seating selection?

OP’s question may suggest the offer of a VP does not bring any benefit to the player offering the VP and is made purely to help somebody else to win.

Messages.Author: Raven
Messages.Body:
According to Tournament Rules Choosing of seating is before Pre-Game Procedure so it is not a part of the game.

Situation that I have mentioned is like trade that for let's say for 1 VP (that means that offering player will be doing things to help another player to gain this 1 VP) another player will take the particular seat, it doesn't guarantee anyone GW, but can greatly influence game and it's outcome overall.

so that's why i'm asking if making such deals before game has even started is legal?

Ankha, do you mean that players are _forbidden_ to make deals outside of the game?

How to prevent two finalists from discussing the finals before seats are chosen and coming to an arrangement? Say, they'll work together to oust a certain other finalist or they won't choose seats next to one another and will work in certain manner during the game.

and this will cause plenty of headache when trying to enforce such a rule.

Messages.Author: Joscha

I don't see a problem here. Table Talk is forbidden while choosing the seating, period. Violating that rule demands a warning, repeated violation means disqualification.
I find it disgusting when I have to listen to thteats issued by a player of a combat deck or other whining. Choose in silence, play the game. Everybody can imagine, how the seating influences the following game without any deal making chatter.
If you let them talk you need rules for that too, for example how long can deal making take or what are you allowed to promise.

> > > Situation that I have mentioned is like trade that for let's say for 1 VP (that means that offering player will be doing things to help another player to gain this 1 VP) another player will take the particular seat, it doesn't guarantee anyone GW, but can greatly influence game and it's outcome overall.

> > >
> > You cannot make deals outside a game, so no.
> >
> Ankha, do you mean that players are _forbidden_ to make deals outside of the game?
>
Yes.

> Lönkka wrote:
> How to prevent two finalists from discussing the finals before seats are chosen and coming to an arrangement?
>
If they do it publicly, the judge can intervene.
If they do it in secret, it's collusion and should be sanctionned.

> Lönkka wrote:
> Say, they'll work together to oust a certain other finalist or they won't choose seats next to one another and will work in certain manner during the game.
>
That's a deal. Deals are not allowed outside the game.

> Lönkka wrote:
> None of the deals in the game are binding in any case and doublecrossing is very common. So why can't the finalists make deals while choosing the seating?
>
Because it's not done during the game.
Deals should be done within the constraint of a game with a time-limit and the PTW aspect in mind. PTW is based on a game-state and is undefined before the game starts (as there is no "play" yet).

> Lönkka wrote:
> Saying that deals can't be made outside the game table seems rather idealistic approach as some people will in any case definitely make some kinds of deals beforehand...
>
That would be cheating.

> Lönkka wrote:
> and this will cause plenty of headache when trying to enforce such a rule.
>
As much as preventing players from collusing or not playing to win.

Keep in mind that all this topic is about dealing. Discussion are allowed but should not lead to any kind of deal.
If the seating takes too long, or if the players tend to haggle over the seating, the judge could decide to disallow further discussion.
